subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Women in Britain gained the vote on the same terms as men in which year?
questions.explain: The 1928 Act extended the vote to all women over 21, on equal terms with men.

questions.q: The Peasants' Revolt of 1381 was triggered largely by which grievance?
questions.explain: Resentment at the Poll Tax sparked the Peasants' Revolt of 1381, led by Wat Tyler.

questions.q: During the Peasants' Revolt of 1381, who was the rebels' main leader killed at Smithfield?
questions.explain: Wat Tyler led the rebels and was killed during the confrontation with Richard II at Smithfield.

questions.q: The Suffragettes, led by Emmeline Pankhurst, were known for what type of campaign?
options: Militant, direct action such as protests and hunger strikes
questions.explain: The Suffragettes (WSPU) used militant tactics, unlike the law-abiding Suffragists.

questions.q: In 1918, the Representation of the People Act gave the vote to which women?
options: Women over 30 who met a property qualification
Only women who had served in the war
questions.explain: The 1918 Act gave the vote to women over 30 with a property qualification; equality came in 1928.

questions.q: Magna Carta, which limited the power of the king, was sealed by King John in which year?
questions.explain: King John sealed Magna Carta in 1215 after pressure from rebellious barons.

questions.q: King Charles I was tried and executed in which year following the English Civil War?
questions.explain: Charles I was executed in 1649, the only English king to be put on trial and beheaded.

questions.q: The General Strike took place in Britain in which year?
questions.explain: The General Strike of 1926 saw millions stop work in support of the coal miners.

questions.q: The Tolpuddle Martyrs of 1834 were punished for doing what?
questions.explain: Six Dorset labourers were transported for swearing a secret oath to form a trade union.

questions.q: The 'Glorious Revolution' of 1688 led to which key constitutional document the following year?
questions.explain: The 1689 Bill of Rights limited royal power and strengthened Parliament after 1688.

questions.q: The Great Reform Act of 1832 did what?
options: Redistributed seats and modestly widened the franchise
questions.explain: The 1832 Reform Act removed some 'rotten boroughs' and extended the vote to more middle-class men.

questions.q: The Chartists of the 1830s-40s campaigned mainly for what?
options: Political reforms including votes for all men
questions.explain: The People's Charter demanded reforms such as universal manhood suffrage and a secret ballot.
